etymology_text:
Of uncertain origin. Has been linked to Latin vagus (“wandering, roaming”); wandering vagrants were perhaps considered to be more likely to steal, or perhaps the act of stealing could be viewed as a "wandering off" of goods.
The present-tense forms are from the o-grade stem vag-, while the non-present-tense forms are from the lengthened o-grade stem *wāg-.
